$comment: TypeScript 7 (the Go port) no longer auto-discovers node_modules/@types.
Under TypeScript 5.9 this program silently picked up every package in
node_modules/@types — exactly these four — and the `types` field below
reproduces that set verbatim, so the program means the same thing under
both compilers. Measured: with this list, `tsc 5.9.3` and `tsc 7.0.2`
report identical diagnostics for this program (0 errors each); without it,
TypeScript 7 reports 109 errors, all of them "Cannot find name
'node:fs'"-shaped, caused by @types/node simply not being loaded.
MAINTENANCE: the list is explicit now, so adding a new @types/*
dependency means adding it here too. The failure direction is safe — a
missing entry produces EXTRA errors, never missing ones. The same list
is repeated in each packages/*/tsconfig.json, which are standalone
programs and do not inherit this file.
The exclude above keeps the reserved probe files out of this program.
A guard test plants a throwaway probe in the working tree to prove a
layer rule is armed, and deletes it again. If tsc's program contains such
a file, two things go wrong: the probe's body is not necessarily valid
TypeScript (it names modules the package does not depend on), and the
probe can be deleted between tsc listing the file and reading it, which
is TS6053. Both failures belong to the probe, not to the tree.
packages/ui/tsconfig.json and packages/backend-client/tsconfig.json carry
the same exclude: fixing only the root config leaves the per-package
programs able to see a probe.
